subject: Audit & Access Logs: export windows, deletion API, and SLA implications
body:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fincocap.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@acme-sec.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Audit / access logs — retention window & export capabilities

Hi Sergio,

Quick question from our security team as we prepare for a vendor security review: what exactly is included in Redwood's audit + access logs, how long you retain them by default, and what export capabilities we have for long-term archival? Specifically:

- Which events are captured (auth successes/failures, token use, model request metadata, request/response headers) — do logs include requester IP and user identifiers?
- What are the default retention periods for (a) platform audit logs (admin actions), (b) access/request logs (per API call), and (c) KV/audit caches if relevant?
- Can we export raw logs (parquet/JSON) to an S3 bucket on a scheduled basis? Any streaming/export SLA?
- Is there a deletion API for data subject requests and how does that interact with audit records?

If you can point me at docs or provide a short summary we can include in our questionnaire. Appreciated.

Thanks,
Tom
Security Operations
FinCo Capital

On Thu, 4 Jun 2026 11:05:42 -0400, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fincocap.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Audit / access logs — retention window & export capabilities

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica from CS and Lauren for any account-level notes. Below is a concise summary and attached playbook we usually share with customers; happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through.

Short answers first:
- Events captured: auth attempts (success/fail), API request metadata (timestamp, model, route, latency, tokens_in/out), request origin (IP), user_agent, API key identifier (hashed), and high-level request/response sizes. We do not persist full request payloads by default; payloads are logged as metadata fields only unless you enable request logging for debug (explicit opt-in).
- Default retention: platform audit events (admin console actions, IAM changes) = 25 months; access/request logs = 13 months; temporary KV cache traces = 90 days.
- Export: yes — scheduled export to a customer S3 is supported (daily or hourly batches). Exports are JSON Lines or parquet; export SLA for delivery is 24 hours for daily, streaming options available for enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Deletion API: we provide a data deletion workflow and a selective deletion API for user-level data. Audit records needed for compliance are redacted rather than removed (we can pseudonymize identifiers). Deletion requests for personal data follow the retention vs compliance hold rules.

Attachments included: redwood_audit_log_export_options.pdf (summary of formats/SLA), SOC2-summary.pdf. See also: https://drive.google.com/finco/redwood-export-playbook (playbook with sample Athena schemas and example parquet mappings).

If you have specific S3 prefixes or a retention policy longer than 13 months, we can discuss a Dedicated export pipeline or a managed archival job via customer-managed S3 with lifecycle rules.

— Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sergio,

Thanks — helpful. A couple of follow-ups our GRC team raised after reviewing the attachments:

1) The retention split of 13 months for request logs is borderline for our legal/compliance requirements — they want 36 months. Is there a self-service way for us to extend retention for access logs in the hosted product, or would that require a Dedicated contract?

2) For the deletion API: if we ask for a user-level deletion, will the corresponding entries in exported archives still contain identifying information? We need to ensure that exported archives are subject to the same deletion workflow.

3) For the export format — do exported logs include hashed API key identifiers that tie back to customer-side ids? We need deterministic linking but not plaintext keys.

Could you have Monica provide detailed answers for 1–3 and a snippet of the export manifest so our infra team can validate ingestion?

— Tom

On Mon, 7 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0400, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fincocap.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Audit / access logs — retention window & export capabilities

Hi Tom — Monica here (Customer Success, infra compliance). Apologies for the delayed reply — pulled together specifics below and added an export manifest example attached (export-playbook-steps.docx).

1) Retention extension:
- Hosted (standard): retention windows are fixed (13 months for request logs) to keep the shared-hosted tier performant and cost-effective.
- Options to reach 36 months:
  - Dedicated: reserved capacity with a configurable retention policy; typical setup includes a managed export pipeline to your S3 with 36+ month retention and lifecycle rules.
  - Hosted + managed archival: we offer a paid add-on to stream exports to your customer-owned S3 where you can set a 36-month lifecycle — logs are available in raw form there indefinitely per your bucket policy. This is generally the fastest path without moving to Dedicated.

2) Deletion API and exported archives:
- Deletion semantics: the deletion API removes or pseudonymizes identifiers in live Redwood storage and marks records as redacted for compliance holds.
- Exports: when we export logs to a customer S3, we treat that output as customer-controlled data. If you require that exported logs are subject to Redwood-managed deletions, we can configure the export job to apply pseudonymization rules before write (hashing and salted IDs with customer-provided salt for deterministic mapping). That setting is part of the export job config (see playbook).
- Important: once an export lands in your S3 (customer-owned), Redwood cannot delete objects from that bucket unless we have an explicit cross-account contract and write permissions. For compliance, customers typically set bucket lifecycle or object tagging and a process for deletion upon request. We can assist setting up the hook.

3) API key identifiers and determinism:
- Export format includes a hashed_api_key_id field (SHA256 with configurable salt). We support customer-supplied salt so you can deterministically map hashed ids back to your internal records without Redwood storing plaintext keys. The export manifest includes the hashing algorithm and salt_id reference.

Export manifest snippet (example from export-playbook-steps.docx):
- file_type: parquet
- partition_by: yyyy/MM/dd
- fields: [timestamp, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, hashed_api_key_id, source_ip, user_agent, model, request_id]
- hashing: {algorithm: SHA256, salt_reference: SALT_ID_12345}
- redaction: {payloads: omitted, pii_fields: pseudonymized}

Next steps: I can schedule a short technical call with our infra engineering to walk through the playbook and sample parquet -> Athena schema mapping. If you want the managed archival route, we can provision a sample export job to a FinCo test bucket for validation (requires an IAM role/trust).

Attachments: export-playbook-steps.docx (manifest + sample), redwood_audit_log_export_options.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Best,
Monica Patel

Redwood Inference
